jen_cs: Quick handoff for Aurelia Systems private/VPC rollout. Network peerings and routes are in place but theyre blocked on two items: our service failing to read encrypted config (KMS errors) and their security team wants written evidence of 730d immutable audit retention to avoid a contract clause hold.
devin_se: Can you paste the exact KMS error from their agent logs?
jen_cs: They sent: `KMS AccessDenied: Not authorized to perform kms:Decrypt on key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:999888777666:key/ee11-22aa-33bb`. Happens when pods call /v1/secrets/unseal.
rachel_kms: Sounds like a key policy or missing grant. Two possibilities: (1) They manage the CMK in their account and Redwood needs to be whitelisted in the key policy (principal or condition on SourceAccount). (2) They use a key in Redwood account and the node role needs explicit decrypt permissions. Ask whether the CMK has key policy with a wildcard principal or restrictive IAM only.
noah_net: Also check the node's IRSA/EC2 role. We often see eks serviceaccount or instance role lacking `kms:Decrypt` or missing `kms:GenerateDataKey`.
jen_cs: They confirmed the key is in their account. Sent role ARN `arn:aws:iam::222333444555:role/aurelia-infer-role` and key ARN above. I replied with a minimal role policy snippet for them to attach to node role:

```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:DescribeKey"],"Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:999888777666:key/ee11-22aa-33bb"}
  ]
}
```

rachel_kms: For the key policy, recommend an explicit statement like below (they own the key):

```
{
  "Sid":"AllowRedwoodServiceAccount",
  "Effect":"Allow",
  "Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::555666777888:role/redwood-service-role"},
  "Action":["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey*"],
  "Condition":{"StringEquals":{"aws:SourceAccount":"555666777888"}}
}
```

rachel_kms: Also point them at a short Grant flow if they want to keep tightly scoped key policy: 1) call CreateGrant with GranteePrincipal set to our service role ARN, 2) Operations Encrypt/Decrypt and RetireGrant false, 3) use GrantToken if needed. Grants can help when you don't want to change policy.

devin_se: For debug, ask them to run a direct decrypt from a node and paste the full AWS error with request-id. We can correlate in our logs. Example test to run inside node: `echo "$(aws kms encrypt --key-id <key-arn> --plaintext hello --query CiphertextBlob --output text)" | base64 --decode > /tmp/ct.bin && aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb:///tmp/ct.bin`

jen_cs: Moving to audit logs: Aurelia wants Splunk HEC ingestion via Firehose from CloudTrail->S3->Firehose. Their security team requires immutability proof for 730 days. They asked whether enabling S3 Object Lock + Versioning is sufficient and how that interacts with lifecycle rules.
noah_net: Object Lock (WORM) + Versioning is the standard ask. Important notes: once Object Lock is turned on for a bucket it requires a retention mode (GOVERNANCE or COMPLIANCE) and that affects deletion/retention. Lifecycle transitions to GLACIER are fine but you cannot shorten retention below the locked period. We'll need them to confirm they own the enforcement and that no lifecycle rule overwrites immutability.

jen_cs: They said theyll enable versioning but didnt want Object Lock without review. Security asked for a written attestation from us that logs will be stored and retained 730 days in their bucket once account settings are applied. They want sample bucket policy and Firehose role.
devin_se: Sample minimal Firehose role trust and S3 put statement (replace ARNs):

```
# Firehose role inline policy
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Statement":[
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["s3:PutObject","s3:PutObjectAcl","s3:ListBucket"],"Resource":["arn:aws:s3:::aurelia-audit/*","arn:aws:s3:::aurelia-audit"]}
  ]
}
```

and bucket policy to allow Firehose principal to PutObject: 
```
{
  "Version":"2012-10-17",
  "Statement":[
    {"Effect":"Allow","Principal":{"AWS":"arn:aws:iam::555666777888:role/firehose-deliver-role"},"Action":"s3:PutObject","Resource":"arn:aws:s3:::aurelia-audit/*","Condition":{}}
  ]
}
```

noah_net: Also recommend server-side encryption for the bucket (`SSE-KMS`) pointing at their CMK and add `s3:ObjectLockRetention` tags to objects if they go that route.

jen_cs: CS renewal note: customer asked for verification by Monday EOD. They indicated procurement may delay contract renewal if compliance sign-off for audit retention is missing. I've flagged as 'at-risk' in tracker. If we don't have confirmed KMS decrypt and written retention attestation by Monday 5pm PT, escalate to CSM lead.

rachel_kms: Action items I'll own: (1) Draft a 1-page KMS checklist (key policy statement + grant example + test command) and share in thread; (2) Verify what the Redwood service principal ARN should be in their policy.
devin_se: I'll produce a 1-page Firehose/S3 bullets for their security team (role ARNs, bucket policy, note about Object Lock implications).
noah_net: I'll join the call if they want network/Firehose walkthrough.
